About:

Kam walks you through the complete process of shipping your first product to Amazon FBA — from creating your shipping plan to getting your inventory checked in and available for sale.

- UPC vs FNSKU barcodes — what each one does and which one must be on every unit before it reaches Amazon
- The cheapest FNSKU labeling strategy — how to avoid Amazon's 55-cent per unit labeling fee by designing the barcode directly onto your packaging or having your manufacturer apply it
- Box templates — setting dimensions, weight limits (under 50 lbs), and unit limits (under 150 per box)
- Amazon Fulfillment Centers vs. Amazon Warehousing and Distribution (AWD) — the difference and when to use each
- Number of warehouses — how splitting shipments affects your placement fees and product availability
- Shipping methods — Small Parcel Delivery vs. Less Than Truckload (LTL) for pallet shipments
Carrier options — Amazon's preferred UPS carrier vs. your own (FedEx, DHL, USPS)
- Placement fees, prep fees, and shipping costs — what to expect before accepting charges
- Printing your UPS and FBA box labels — and why every single box needs both
- Tracking your shipment — from "ready to ship" to "in transit" to "checked in" to "available for sale"
- Common mistakes — wrong ship-from address, missing FNSKU labels, sending too much inventory, and skipping the Bill of Lading for pallet shipments
- Long-term storage fees — how to avoid Amazon's charges by managing your inventory turnover wisely

Kam covers everything Amazon FBA sellers need to know about sending inventory to Amazon warehouses, including barcode labeling strategies, freight forwarding for overseas shipments, processing timelines (3–6 weeks), and how to follow up with Amazon Seller Support if your shipment is delayed or lost.
